vulnerability_analysis: The MarvinInu contract has owner-only functions updateBuyFees() and updateSellFees() that allow setting fees up to 50%. The owner can set fees to the maximum, then perform trades to extract excessive fees. The fees accumulate in the contract and are distributed to marketingWallet and devWallet (both initially set to owner address). By setting fees to 50% and trading with victim addresses, the attacker can siphon funds from victims through the fee mechanism.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Enable trading if not already enabled. 3. Set both buy and sell fees to maximum (50%). 4. Create victim addresses with MARVIN tokens. 5. Perform buy/sell trades with victims to trigger fee collection. 6. Trigger swapBack() to convert tokens to ETH. 7. Collect ETH from marketing/dev wallets (which are attacker-controlled).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call enableTrading() if trading is not active. 3. Call updateBuyFees() and updateSellFees() with 50% total fees each. 4. Create victim addresses and give them MARVIN tokens using deal(). 5. Have victims buy MARVIN tokens (pay ETH, get tokens with 50% fee). 6. Have victims sell MARVIN tokens (pay tokens, get ETH with 50% fee). 7. Trigger swapBack() by transferring tokens to accumulate enough for swap threshold. 8. Collect ETH from marketingWallet and devWallet.
